subject: Islamic Studies
q: Surah Al-Baqarah derives its name from:
o: The cattle of the Prophet Salih (AS)
The Golden Calf of the Samiri
The cow the Children of Israel were commanded to slaughter
explanation: Al-Baqarah relates how Musa (AS) told the Children of Israel to slaughter a cow and how they delayed with repeated questions.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The verse ‘This day I have perfected your religion for you’ was revealed on the occasion of:
explanation: According to Sahih al-Bukhari this verse of Surah Al-Ma’idah was revealed at Arafat on the Day of Arafah during the Farewell Hajj.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Wahi Matlu’ (recited revelation) refers to:
explanation: The Qur’an is recited revelation whose words are from Allah and recited in Salah; the Sunnah is called Wahi Ghair Matlu.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The command to leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of Allah when the call is made on Friday is given in Surah:
explanation: Surah Al-Jumu‘ah commands believers to hasten to Friday prayer and leave off trade, then disperse in the land after it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: It is a Sunnah to recite which Surah on Fridays?
explanation: Hadith report that whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on Friday will have light between two Fridays.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Tafsir al-Kabir (Mafatih al-Ghayb) was written by:
explanation: Fakhr-ud-Din al-Razi’s vast commentary is known for its theological and philosophical discussion of the verses.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: In the recitation of the Qur’an, a stop or pause at the end of a word is called:
explanation: Tajweed lays down rules of Waqf (stopping) and Wasl (joining) so that the meaning is not distorted.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The literal meaning of ‘Hadith’ is:
explanation: Hadith literally means speech, news or a report; technically it is a report of the sayings, actions or approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The literal meaning of ‘Sunnah’ is:
explanation: Sunnah literally means a trodden path or established practice; in Islam it is the way of life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: ‘Hadith Taqriri’ refers to:
o: An act done in the Prophet’s presence which he approved by silence
An action performed by the Prophet (PBUH)
A report narrated by a Successor
explanation: Taqrir means approval: when the Prophet (PBUH) saw or heard something and did not object, his silence made it permissible.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith describing an action of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is called:
explanation: Hadith are classified by content into Qawli (sayings), Fi‘li (actions) and Taqriri (tacit approvals).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) conveys, in his own words, something from Allah is called:
explanation: In a Hadith Qudsi the meaning is from Allah and the wording is the Prophet’s (PBUH); unlike the Qur’an it is not recited in Salah as scripture.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The chain of narrators of a Hadith is called:
explanation: The Isnad (Sanad) is the chain through which a report reaches us; Muslim scholars examined every link to judge authenticity.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The actual text of a Hadith, as distinct from its chain of narrators, is called:
explanation: Every Hadith has two parts: the Isnad (chain) and the Matn (text or content).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith narrated at every stage by so many people that their agreeing on a lie is inconceivable is called:
explanation: Mutawatir reports are transmitted by large numbers in every generation and yield certain knowledge.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith that fails to meet the conditions of acceptance because of a weakness in its chain is called:
explanation: A Da‘if (weak) Hadith lacks one or more conditions of a Sahih or Hasan report, such as continuity or reliable narrators.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The term ‘Hasan’ as a distinct grade of Hadith, between Sahih and Da‘if, was popularised by:
explanation: Imam Tirmidhi regularly graded Hadith as Hasan in his Jami‘, making it a standard category of acceptable Hadith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A fabricated report falsely attributed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is called:
explanation: Mawdu‘ means fabricated; the Prophet (PBUH) warned that whoever deliberately lies about him should prepare his seat in the Fire.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith whose chain goes back to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself is called:
explanation: Marfu‘ means raised: the report is attributed directly to the Prophet (PBUH), whereas Mawquf stops at a Companion and Maqtu‘ at a Successor.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A report attributed to a Companion (Sahabi) rather than to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is called:
explanation: Mawquf means stopped: its chain stops at a Companion and does not reach the Prophet (PBUH).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A report whose chain ends with a Tabi‘i (Successor) is called:
explanation: Maqtu‘ reports convey the words or deeds of a Successor; they are not Prophetic Hadith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith in which a Tabi‘i narrates directly from the Holy Prophet (PBUH), omitting the Companion, is called:
explanation: In a Mursal report the link between the Successor and the Prophet (PBUH) is missing; jurists differ on accepting such reports.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith recorded by both Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim is called:
explanation: Muttafaq ‘Alayh (agreed upon) denotes a Hadith reported by both Bukhari and Muslim, the highest level of authenticity among Ahad reports.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The collective name for the six major Sunni collections of Hadith is:
explanation: The Sihah Sittah are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasa’i and Ibn Majah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are together known as:
explanation: Sahihayn means “the two Sahihs”; Sihah Sittah is the wider set of six books and Sunan Arba‘ah the four Sunan.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which book of Hadith was compiled by Imam Malik?
explanation: Imam Malik of Madinah compiled Al-Muwatta, one of the earliest surviving collections of Hadith and legal practice. Kitab al-Umm is Imam Shafi‘i’s work.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith collection arranged under the names of the Companions who narrated the reports is called a:
explanation: In a Musnad, such as Musnad Ahmad, Hadith are grouped under each Companion narrator rather than by subject.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Imam Bukhari’s personal name was:
explanation: Imam Muhammad bin Isma‘il al-Bukhari compiled his Sahih after years of travel; Muhammad bin Isa is Tirmidhi and Ahmad bin Shu‘aib is Nasa’i.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which of the following collections is NOT one of the Sihah Sittah?
explanation: Musnad Ahmad is a vast and important collection, but it is not counted among the six canonical books.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Mishkat al-Masabih, a popular Hadith anthology, was compiled by:
explanation: Khatib al-Tabrizi expanded al-Baghawi’s Masabih al-Sunnah into Mishkat al-Masabih, widely taught in South Asian madrasas.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Riyad-us-Salihin was compiled by:
explanation: Imam Yahya bin Sharaf al-Nawawi compiled Riyad-us-Salihin, a collection of Hadith on ethics and devotion.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Bulugh al-Maram, a collection of Hadith on legal rulings, was compiled by:
explanation: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani compiled Bulugh al-Maram, arranging Hadith related to Fiqh by legal topics.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Fath al-Bari is a famous commentary on:
explanation: Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani’s Fath al-Bari is regarded as the greatest commentary (sharh) on Sahih al-Bukhari.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The famous collection known as ‘Al-Arba‘in’, containing about forty basic Ahadith, was compiled by:
explanation: Imam Nawawi’s Arba‘in gathers core Hadith on faith, worship and conduct, beginning with “Actions are by intentions”.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Umayyad Caliph issued orders for the official collection of Hadith?
explanation: Fearing the loss of knowledge as scholars passed away, Umar bin Abdul Aziz ordered governors and scholars to record the Hadith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Who is regarded as the first formal compiler (Mudawwin) of Hadith under official patronage?
explanation: Acting on the order of Umar bin Abdul Aziz, Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri systematically recorded Hadith, earning the title of first Mudawwin.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Sahifa Hammam bin Munabbih, one of the earliest surviving written Hadith collections, contains reports narrated from:
explanation: Hammam bin Munabbih wrote down reports from his teacher Abu Hurayrah (RA); Dr. Muhammad Hamidullah edited and published the manuscript.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which Companion narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
explanation: Abu Hurayrah (RA) stayed constantly with the Prophet (PBUH) and is the most prolific narrator of Hadith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Among the wives of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the largest number of Ahadith were narrated by:
explanation: Aisha (RA) is among the most prolific narrators of Hadith and was consulted by Companions on law and the Sunnah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The science that examines the lives and reliability of Hadith narrators is called:
explanation: Asma-ur-Rijal records the biographies, teachers, students and reliability of narrators so that chains can be verified.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The discipline of judging narrators as reliable or unreliable is known as:
explanation: Jarh means criticism and Ta‘dil accreditation; this discipline grades narrators, forming the basis of Hadith authentication.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A scholar who specialises in the science of Hadith is called:
explanation: A Muhaddith studies, transmits and evaluates Hadith; a Mufassir interprets the Qur’an and a Faqih specialises in law.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith that does not reach the level of Tawatur is classified as:
explanation: Ahad reports are those narrated by fewer transmitters than Mutawatir; most Hadith fall into this category.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Sahih al-Bukhari opens with the Hadith:
o: “The Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand others are safe”
explanation: Imam Bukhari began his Sahih with “Innamal a‘malu bin-niyyat”, stressing that sincerity underlies every act.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Hadith ‘Actions are judged by intentions’ was narrated by:
explanation: This Hadith reaches us through Umar bin al-Khattab (RA), who narrated it from the pulpit.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Complete the Hadith: ‘The best of you are those who learn the Qur’an and ______.’
explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari reports: “The best of you are those who learn the Qur’an and teach it.”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Hadith ‘Ad-Din an-Nasihah’ teaches that religion is:
explanation: In Sahih Muslim the Prophet (PBUH) said religion is Nasihah: sincerity towards Allah, His Book, His Messenger, the leaders and the people.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a Sahih Hadith, which quality is a branch of Iman?
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said that faith has many branches and that Haya is one of them (Bukhari, Muslim).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The famous Hadith-e-Jibril explains which three dimensions of the Din?
explanation: When Jibril came in human form, the Prophet (PBUH) explained Islam, Iman and Ihsan and then said, “He came to teach you your religion.”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Sunnah is often described as:
explanation: The Qur’an says the Prophet (PBUH) does not speak of his own desire; his guidance is revelation in meaning, though not recited as the Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The Qur’anic phrase ‘Uswatun Hasanah’ describes the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as:
explanation: Surah Al-Ahzab says: “Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example”, which establishes the authority of his Sunnah.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Imam Muslim, compiler of Sahih Muslim, belonged to:
explanation: Imam Muslim bin al-Hajjaj was from Nishapur in Khurasan and was a student of Imam Bukhari.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Imam Bukhari was born in Bukhara, a city in present-day:
explanation: Bukhara, from which Imam Bukhari takes his name, lies in present-day Uzbekistan.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Hadith collections called ‘Sunan’ mainly contain:
o: Legal Ahadith arranged by topics of Fiqh
explanation: Sunan works such as Abu Dawud and Nasa’i concentrate on Hadith relevant to legal rulings, arranged in chapters of Fiqh.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a Hadith, none of you truly believes until he:
o: Loves for his brother what he loves for himself
Gives all his wealth in charity
explanation: This Hadith in Bukhari and Muslim makes selfless concern for others a condition of complete faith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a Hadith, a true Muslim is one from whose:
o: Tongue and hand other Muslims are safe
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) defined a Muslim as one from whose tongue and hand other Muslims are safe (Bukhari).

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Complete the Hadith: ‘Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or ______.’
explanation: This Hadith in Bukhari and Muslim teaches control of the tongue as a sign of faith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The study of a Hadith’s meaning and soundness of content, as distinct from the transmission of its chain, is called:
explanation: Ilm-ur-Riwayah concerns the transmission of Hadith, while Ilm-ud-Dirayah concerns the rules for understanding and evaluating it.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Muslim who met a Companion but not the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is called:
explanation: A Tabi‘i (Successor) belongs to the generation after the Companions; the next generation is the Taba‘ Tabi‘in.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The word ‘Muwatta’ literally means:
explanation: Imam Malik named his work Al-Muwatta, the smoothed or well-trodden path, reflecting its clear arrangement of Hadith and practice.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Among Sunni scholars, which book is generally regarded as the most authentic after the Qur’an?
explanation: Because of Imam Bukhari’s strict conditions, the majority of Sunni scholars regard his Sahih as the most authentic book after the Qur’an.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Imam Bukhari’s condition, stricter than that of Imam Muslim, required that consecutive narrators:
o: Be proven to have actually met each other
explanation: Imam Muslim accepted contemporaneity with the possibility of meeting, whereas Bukhari required proof that narrators actually met.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: According to a Hadith in Sahih Muslim, purification (Taharah) is:
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said “At-tuhuru shatr-ul-iman”, purity is half of faith.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Complete the Hadith: ‘Du‘a is ______.’
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said “Ad-du‘a’u huwal-‘ibadah” (Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud) and then recited the verse “Call upon Me, I will respond to you.”

subject: Islamic Studies
q: A Hadith narrated by at least three narrators at every stage, but short of Tawatur, is called:
explanation: Among Ahad reports, Mashhur has three or more narrators at each stage, Aziz at least two, and Gharib only one at some stage.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: The first pillar of Islam is:
explanation: The Hadith “Islam is built on five” lists first the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad (PBUH) is His Messenger.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which pillar of Islam is primarily a financial act of worship?
explanation: Zakat is an obligatory share of wealth paid to prescribed recipients; Salah and Sawm are bodily acts of worship.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which act of worship is both physical and financial?
explanation: Hajj requires bodily effort in its rites and also the financial means to travel and provide for dependants.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which obligatory act of worship is required only once in a lifetime of those who are able?
explanation: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime upon every adult Muslim who has the physical and financial ability.

subject: Islamic Studies
q: Which act of worship is described in a Hadith as the dividing line between a believer and disbelief?
explanation: Sahih Muslim reports that between a man and disbelief stands the abandonment of prayer, showing Salah’s central place.
